title: Survey participation can improve through targeted design changes while broader response still declines
source_unit: U.S. Census Bureau 2026 ACS Research and Evaluation Report Memorandum Series #ACS26-RER-01, summarizing self-response contact-strategy research from 2005–2025
geography: United States American Community Survey housing-unit collection; Puerto Rico is excluded from the report's contact-strategy discussion

denominator.unit: ACS monthly panels and weighted self-response rates

item_quality.value: Sequential layout significantly reduced person-incompleteness and some discrepancies

observations.method: Census evaluation comparing the sequential demographic layout with the prior grid layout and comparing 2008 monthly panels with corresponding 2007 panels.
observations.uncertainty: The effect is tied to a questionnaire-layout change and production context; it does not establish equal response improvement for every subgroup or later data-use quality.
observations.subgroup: ACS sampled housing units and household responses; detailed subgroup effects are not retained in this record.
observations.counterinterpretation: A higher response rate can coexist with burden, item nonresponse, or unequal participation among harder-to-reach households.

denominator.unit: ACS monthly panels and weighted self-response rates

internet_option.value: Adding an internet response option was associated with higher self-response

observations.method: Census evaluation of the internet response option and related contact-strategy changes, comparing 2013 panels with corresponding 2012 panels.
observations.uncertainty: The report notes operational disruption from a government shutdown in October 2013; the comparison is not a universal estimate of digital access or data quality.
observations.subgroup: ACS sampled housing units by monthly panel and response mode; subgroup mechanisms remain paper-specific.
observations.counterinterpretation: Digital access can lower some response costs while creating device, literacy, language, privacy, or security barriers for others.

denominator.unit: ACS monthly panels and weighted self-response rates

observations.method: Census comparison of 2015 panels after the mail-contact change with 2014 panels.
observations.uncertainty: The source describes a program-era comparison, not a linked household-level pathway from message receipt to response motivation or later civic participation.
observations.subgroup: ACS sampled housing units; subgroup response and burden differences are not extracted.
observations.counterinterpretation: A modest aggregate increase can conceal unequal effects across geography, language, housing stability, and trust in government.

denominator.unit: ACS April–December monthly panels compared with corresponding 2021 panels

self_response_change.unit: three higher, three lower, and three not statistically different panels

long_run_direction.value: Despite repeated contact-strategy changes, self-response rates continued to decline over the longer period

observations.method: Census comparison of 2022 and 2021 panels, excluding pandemic-affected early 2021 panels from the main comparison.
observations.uncertainty: This is an aggregate panel comparison and does not identify why individual households responded or did not respond.
observations.subgroup: ACS sampled housing units and response panels; detailed subgroup treatment effects remain open.
observations.counterinterpretation: A neutral aggregate test may still help some groups or reduce costs without shifting the overall response rate.

related_sources.claim: Census landing page identifies the report, authors, September 2026 date, and scope from 2005 through 2025.

boundary: This record adds an institutional participation and measurement layer: contact design can change response rates or data-completion indicators, but repeated improvements do not eliminate broader response decline. It does not establish household trust, representativeness, equal burden, policy responsiveness, or political participation, and it does not follow the same household from contact to later outcome.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official Census PDF report and landing page; ACS microdata, paradata, and full response-rate series are not retained.
